title: Shopify App Development Cost in 2026: The Four Fees No Quote Includes
desc: What a Shopify app really costs in 2026. Verified Shopify fees, why 0 percent revenue share is never zero, custom versus public distribution, and the annual API migration no quote mentions.
keywords: shopify app development cost, shopify app development cost 2026, how much does a shopify app cost, cost to build a shopify app, custom shopify app cost, shopify app revenue share, shopify app store fees, hire shopify app developer cost
cta: Want a Shopify app quote that itemizes every cost, not just the build?
body:
The short answer

No blog post can quote you a Shopify app build price, and every guide that tries is quoting its own rate card. What can be pinned down is the part Shopify itself publishes, and that is exactly the part most budgets get wrong. The build fee is a one-time number you negotiate. Shopify's fees are a permanent number you inherit.

Verified on Shopify's own developer documentation on August 6, 2026: registering to sell on the Shopify App Store costs a one-time $19 per Partner account. Revenue share is 0% on your first $1,000,000 of gross app revenue earned since January 1, 2025, then 15% above that. Separately, all billing carries a 2.9% processing fee, plus applicable sales tax.

Three consequences follow that almost no cost guide states plainly:

  • The 0% band was never free. By the time an app has earned that first $1,000,000, it has already handed Shopify $29,000 in processing fees. The fee you get told about is $19. The fee you actually pay to exhaust the free band is roughly 1,500 times larger.
  • The real marginal rate above the threshold is 17.9%, not 15%, because the 2.9% never switches off.
  • The cheapest Shopify app is the one that never enters the App Store. Shopify's own wording: registration "isn't required if you're only developing custom apps for a single merchant." A single-store custom app carries no $19, no revenue share, and no app review.

If you are still deciding whether you need an app at all, start with this plan check before you price anything.

Why every published price range is useless

Search the cost question and you get confident numbers. Read four of them side by side and they stop agreeing. In August 2026 the published guides put freelance Shopify developers at $25 to $70 an hour, at $30 to $285 an hour, and at $45 to $70 an hour for North America. Agency rates appear as $50 to $150, as $60 to $200, and as $100 to $400. A public App Store MVP is quoted anywhere from $30,000 to $150,000.

The top of one range is more than ten times the bottom of another for the same job title. That is not a market with genuine variance in it, that is a set of vendors publishing their own price list as if it were research. Every one of those pages is on the website of a company that sells Shopify development, including, in fairness, ours.

So treat the build quote as a variable you control, not a fact you look up. The rest of this guide is the part you can verify without trusting anybody, because Shopify publishes it.

The four costs Shopify publishes

1. Registration: $19, one time, per Partner account. Paid from the Partner Dashboard before you can distribute a public app. Not required for single-merchant custom apps.

2. Revenue share: 0% then 15%, and the threshold is lifetime. The $1,000,000 allowance counts gross app revenue earned from January 1, 2025 onward, and it does not reset annually. It is also calculated across all of your Associated Developer Accounts, so a second app inherits whatever the first app has already spent. Shopify also states the allowance does not apply at all to developers who earned $20,000,000 or more through the App Store in the prior calendar year, or whose gross company revenue is $100,000,000 or more. Those developers pay 15% from the first dollar.

3. The 2.9% processing fee on all billing. Charged separately from revenue share, so it applies inside the 0% band as well as above it. Earnings in some countries also attract a regulatory operating fee.

4. Hosting, which Shopify does not provide. Shopify's deployment documentation points you at Google Cloud Run or a hosting service of your choice. The App Store is a distribution channel and a billing system. It is not a server. Every request your app serves runs on infrastructure you rent and monitor.

One more line that belongs here because it costs real money and reads like a footnote: revenue share is calculated on gross sales, and refunds are not taken into account. You pay Shopify on money you gave back.

What "0% revenue share" actually costs

Take a plain app at $29 a month with 500 paying merchants. That is $14,500 a month, or $174,000 a year, of gross app revenue.

  • Inside the 0% band you still pay the 2.9% processing fee: $420.50 a month, or $5,046 a year. Nothing about that is zero.
  • Reaching the $1,000,000 threshold takes 34,483 subscription months at $29. At 500 merchants that is about 69 months, roughly five years and nine months. For most apps the 15% is a problem for a future owner, while the 2.9% is a problem on day one. Cost guides invert this constantly.
  • Above the threshold the same $174,000 costs $26,100 in revenue share plus $5,046 in processing, so $31,146 a year, a true rate of 17.9%.
  • Refunds are pure leakage. Refund 5% of that $174,000 and you have returned $8,700 to merchants while still paying $1,305 in revenue share and $252.30 in processing on it. That is $1,557.30 a year charged on money you no longer have.

Every one of those figures is arithmetic on Shopify's published rates. Check them.

The one decision that moves the cost by an order of magnitude

Before anything is built you must choose a distribution method, and Shopify does not let you change it afterwards.

Custom distribution installs your app on one store, or on multiple stores inside the same Plus organization, using an install link you generate in the Partner Dashboard. There is no App Store listing, no app review queue, no listing assets, no revenue share, and no $19. If the app exists to solve one merchant's workflow, this is the correct and dramatically cheaper answer, and it is the answer most agencies quoting a public app never offer.

Public distribution is the App Store. It brings the listing, the review process, the ongoing quality standards, the revenue share, and a permanent marketing job. It is the right choice only if you intend to sell the app as a product to many merchants, which is a business, not a project.

A note that catches people: if you create a custom app through the Shopify admin rather than the Partner Dashboard, you cannot change its distribution method at all. Decide before you write code, not after. If you want that decision pressure-tested against your actual store setup, that is what our Shopify app development team looks at first.

The annual rebuild you cannot decline

This is the line item that turns a project into a subscription, and it is missing from nearly every quote.

Shopify ships a new API version every three months. Each stable version is supported for a minimum of 12 months, with at least nine months of overlap between consecutive versions. The Shopify CLI also blocks deploys targeting UI extension versions older than 12 months, so an app left on a stale version cannot ship a bug fix even if you want to.

The penalty for ignoring it is published and severe. An app still calling unsupported resources after the upgrade deadline is delisted from the Shopify App Store, users are blocked from installing it for a minimum of seven days, and warning banners appear in the merchant's admin until seven days after the last detected use.

There is a live deadline right now. API version 2025-10 stops being accessible on October 16, 2026 at 15:00 UTC, which is 71 days from today. Version 2025-07 already went dark on July 16, 2026.

Budget it as a recurring engineering line, not a contingency. A Shopify app faces at least one forced API migration every year for its entire life. A quote that has no maintenance retainer next to it is not cheaper, it is incomplete.

What an honest quote itemizes

You do not need to know the right price. You need to know whether the quote in front of you covers the work Shopify makes mandatory. Ask for these as separate lines:

  • OAuth and an embedded admin experience, not a link out to a separate web app.
  • The mandatory compliance webhooks Shopify requires for privacy law compliance, plus a real process for handling data access and erasure requests.
  • A published privacy policy linked from the App Store listing. Shopify requires it for both full and limited visibility apps.
  • Billing integration, because charging merchants is code you have to write.
  • Clean uninstall, including theme app extensions for anything that touches the storefront.
  • Hosting, monitoring, and on-call, priced monthly.
  • The annual API migration, priced annually.
  • Listing assets and a support channel, if you are going public.

Two process facts worth setting expectations on. First, Shopify publishes no review turnaround time. The documented flow moves through Draft, Submitted, Paused, Reviewed and Published, and an app that fails core requirements is paused and must be resubmitted, but there is no committed SLA anywhere in the docs. Anyone who promises you a review date is guessing. Second, Built for Shopify status is optional and gated. You apply for it, and if you fail the same criterion three times in a row your application is suspended for three months. Apps that hold the status are re-reviewed annually and get 60 days to fix any failure. It is worth pursuing for the search ranking boost and the priority review queue, but it is a program you maintain, not a badge you buy.

Who should not build a Shopify app

We build these for a living and we still turn this work down regularly. Skip the build if any of the following is true.

An existing App Store app does 80% of it. Paying $49 a month for something imperfect beats owning a codebase with a permanent API migration attached. The honest comparison is not build price versus app price, it is build price plus five years of maintenance versus app price.

The need is one store's workflow and it fits Shopify Flow or Functions. A lot of what gets scoped as an app is automation. If the job is moving data between systems or reacting to store events, look at e-commerce automation before you commission software.

You cannot fund the maintenance line. An app you can afford to build but not to maintain will be delisted within about a year of neglect, and Shopify has published exactly how that happens.

If none of those apply and you genuinely need custom code in the admin or the checkout, the right next step is a scoped conversation, not a number from a search result. That is what we do when you hire a Shopify expert: work out which distribution method you actually need, then price the mandatory scope honestly. If your app will pull external product or competitor data, our guide to e-commerce data tools covers that side of the build.
faqs: How much does it cost to build a Shopify app in 2026?

There is no reliable published range. Guides written by development agencies quote freelance rates anywhere from 25 to 285 dollars an hour and public app MVPs from 30,000 to 150,000 dollars, which is a spread of more than ten times for the same work. What can be verified is Shopify's side: a one-time 19 dollar App Store registration fee per Partner account, 0 percent revenue share on your first 1,000,000 dollars of gross app revenue earned since January 1 2025, 15 percent above that, and a 2.9 percent processing fee on all billing. Price the build by asking a vendor to itemize the mandatory scope rather than by looking up a range.
Does Shopify take a cut of Shopify app revenue?

Yes, for apps distributed through the Shopify App Store. You keep 100 percent of your first 1,000,000 dollars in gross app revenue earned from January 1 2025 onward and 85 percent above that. The threshold is lifetime rather than annual and is calculated across all Associated Developer Accounts, so a second app shares the same allowance. All billing also carries a 2.9 percent processing fee charged separately, which means the true marginal rate above the threshold is 17.9 percent, not 15 percent. Custom apps distributed to a single merchant carry no revenue share.
Is there a fee to publish an app on the Shopify App Store?

Yes. Shopify charges a one-time 19 dollar registration fee per Partner account before you can distribute a public app, paid in the Partner Dashboard. Registration is not required if you are only developing custom apps for a single merchant. There is no separate listing fee, but revenue share and the 2.9 percent processing fee apply once you start billing merchants.
What is the difference between a custom Shopify app and a public app?

A custom app is installed on one store, or on multiple stores within the same Shopify Plus organization, using an install link you generate. It skips the App Store listing, the app review process, the 19 dollar registration and revenue share entirely. A public app is listed on the Shopify App Store, must pass app review, and is subject to revenue share and ongoing quality standards. Shopify does not let you change the distribution method after you select it, so the choice has to be made before development starts.
How long does Shopify app review take?

Shopify publishes no turnaround time or service level for app review. The documented process moves an app through Draft, Submitted, Paused, Reviewed and Published statuses. If your app fails core requirements it moves to Paused and you have to fix the issues and resubmit, which restarts the wait. Developers who already hold Built for Shopify status get a prioritized review queue for future submissions, but the same requirements still apply. Treat any promised review date from a vendor as an estimate, not a commitment.
What are the ongoing costs of a Shopify app after launch?

Four recurring costs, and only one of them is usually quoted. Hosting and monitoring, because Shopify does not host your app and its own docs point you at Google Cloud Run or another hosting service. The 2.9 percent processing fee on every dollar billed, which applies even inside the 0 percent revenue share band. Revenue share of 15 percent once lifetime gross app revenue passes 1,000,000 dollars. And an annual API migration: Shopify releases a version every quarter and supports each stable version for a minimum of 12 months, and an app still calling unsupported resources after the deadline is delisted from the App Store with installs blocked for at least seven days.
